topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the series context, and the lecture's learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology, Risk Factors, and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental biology of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by intrinsic mutational processes, hereditary predisposition, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific biological, physical, and chemical agents drive malignancy through direct DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolic activation, chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and life-stage tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, animal, and bacterial assay methods used to evaluate, prove, and profile the carcinogenic potential of environmental agents.
